title: INR test on warfarin
what: This blood test shows how fast your blood clots. Your doctor uses it to set your warfarin dose.
why: Regularly while you take warfarin: more often at the start, then usually every few weeks.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come the same day
tell_doctor: Your warfarin dose and when you take it
If you missed a pill or took an extra one
If you started any new medicines, antibiotics, or herbs
If your diet changed a lot, especially greens and vegetables
If you drank alcohol or were ill

prepare.title: Warfarin
prepare.text: Take it as usual, at your usual time. Do not change the dose yourself before the test.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually you do not need to fast, but it is best in the morning before a big breakfast. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Records
prepare.text: Keep a log: date, dose, and INR result. Bring it with you.

bring: Your INR and warfarin dose log
steps: Blood is taken from a vein, or sometimes from a fingertip with a quick-test device
From a vein: a band is tightened and there is a quick prick
From a finger: a small prick, and a drop of blood is taken
A cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
after: Press the cotton pad longer, 5 to 10 minutes. On warfarin, bleeding stops more slowly
Your doctor will tell you the result and your new dose
Write the result in your log
red_flags: Black stools, blood in urine or vomit, or a nosebleed that will not stop: call emergency services
A sudden severe headache, or weakness in an arm or leg: call emergency services
Many bruises for no reason: see a doctor in the next few days

faq.q: How often do I need an INR test?
faq.a: Often at first, while the dose is being set. Then usually every few weeks. Your doctor will give you a schedule.

faq.q: Can I eat greens on warfarin?
faq.a: Yes, but about the same amount every day. Sudden diet changes change your INR.

reminders.text: INR test tomorrow. Take warfarin as usual. Bring your dose log.
